guides.title: Brooks Ghost Alternatives: Safe Neutral Trainers Compared
guides.excerpt: The Mizuno Wave Rider 30 is the closest Ghost 18 alternative: $145, 9.8 oz and the same 12 mm drop. The Saucony Ride 19 and ASICS Cumulus 28 are lighter.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** The Mizuno Wave Rider 30 is the closest Brooks Ghost 18 alternative: $145, 9.8 oz and the same 12 mm drop. The Saucony Ride 19 is lighter at 9.3 oz.

## The Ghost 18 is the benchmark

The [Ghost 18](/shoes/brooks-ghost-18) is $150 and 9.8 oz with a 36 mm stack and a 12 mm drop. Our data lists it as dependable, durable and a fit for most feet, with wide sizes. The weaknesses are little energy return and a firmer ride than max-cushion shoes.

## Same drop and same job

The [Mizuno Wave Rider 30](/shoes/mizuno-wave-rider-30) is $145 and 9.8 oz with a 38 mm stack and a 12 mm drop. It has a stable, structured ride and is built for high mileage. It is not soft enough for runners who want a plush recovery shoe.

The Nike Pegasus 42 is $145 and 9.8 oz with a 37 mm stack and a 10 mm drop. See our [Pegasus alternatives guide](/rundown/nike-pegasus-alternatives) for its own rivals.

## Lighter with an 8 mm drop

- [Saucony Ride 19](/shoes/saucony-ride-19): $145, 9.3 oz, 35 mm stack. Balanced cushion and a durable upper.
- [ASICS Gel-Cumulus 28](/shoes/asics-gel-cumulus-28): $145, 9.2 oz, 38 mm stack. Light for its cushion with an accommodating fit.
- New Balance Fresh Foam X 880 v15: $140, 10.4 oz, 36 mm stack. Heavier but available in several widths.

Moving from 12 mm to 8 mm is a small change. Our [heel drop guide](/rundown/heel-drop-explained-4mm-vs-10mm) covers how to ramp up if your calves feel it.

## Cheaper or softer within the same brand

- Brooks Revel 9: $100, 8.7 oz, 33 mm stack, 8 mm drop. Firm and basic, good for short daily runs.
- Brooks Glycerin 23: $165, 10.1 oz, 38 mm stack, 10 mm drop. The plush Brooks.
- Brooks Ghost Max 4: $160, 10.3 oz, 39 mm stack, 6 mm drop. More protection, too heavy for workouts.

## If the Ghost is the wrong shape

Runners who overpronate and want built-in support should read our [stability vs neutral guide](/rundown/stability-shoes-vs-neutral-do-you-need-support). The Adrenaline GTS 26 is $155 and 10.8 oz, the support version in the same brand.

Runners who want a softer, taller ride should look at the Hoka Clifton 11 instead. The [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector) narrows the list by fit and cushion.

guides.title: Hoka Clifton Alternatives: Soft Daily Trainers That Cost Less or Fit Wider
guides.excerpt: The ASICS Novablast 6 is $150 like the Clifton 11 and weighs 0.7 oz less. The Saucony Procyon Max is the max-cushion option at $120.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** The ASICS Novablast 6 is the best Hoka Clifton alternative: same $150 price, 9.0 oz against 9.7 oz, and a 41 mm stack. For a roomier fit, the Topo Phantom 4 has a wide toe box.

## The Clifton 11 is the benchmark

The [Clifton 11](/shoes/hoka-clifton-11) is $150 and 9.7 oz with a 42 mm stack and an 8 mm drop. Our data lists it as plush and rockered, good for walking and standing, with ordinary EVA foam and no versatility at faster paces. Our [Clifton 11 vs Ghost 18 guide](/rundown/hoka-clifton-11-vs-brooks-ghost-18) compares it to its main rival.

## The Novablast 6 is lighter and bouncier

The [Novablast 6](/shoes/asics-novablast-6) keeps a tall 41 mm stack and the same 8 mm drop at $150. It weighs 9.0 oz and is listed as light for its cushion with an energetic ride.

It is not the most stable platform. Runners who want a planted feel should choose another shoe from this list.

## More cushion, softer foam or a lower price

- [Nike Vomero 18](/shoes/nike-vomero-18): $150, 10.5 oz, 46 mm stack, 10 mm drop. Taller and softer, heavier.
- Saucony Triumph 24: $170, 9.7 oz, 37 mm stack, 10 mm drop. Plush PEBA foam, a higher price.
- ASICS Gel-Nimbus 28: $165, 10.6 oz, 43 mm stack, 8 mm drop. Plush and durable, a heavy shoe.
- [Saucony Procyon Max](/shoes/saucony-procyon-max): $120, 10.7 oz, 38 mm stack, 6 mm drop. Max cushion on a budget, stable and broad.

## Wider fit or a different drop

The [Topo Athletic Phantom 4](/shoes/topo-athletic-phantom-4) is $150 and 9.5 oz with a 35 mm stack, a 5 mm drop and a wide, anatomical toe box. Its ZipFoam is less lively than newer foams.

The Hoka Arahi 9 is $150 and 9.7 oz with an 8 mm drop and a roomier forefoot than the Arahi 8. It adds light stability from a J-Frame guide. Our [wide feet guide](/rundown/wide-feet-running-shoes) lists more roomy options.

## Who should stay with the Clifton

Runners who stand or walk all day in their shoes should keep the Clifton. The rocker and 42 mm stack are built for that, and the alternatives above are tuned more for running.

If the Clifton feels too soft and slow for tempo days, add a lighter second pair rather than replacing it. The [shoe rotation guide](/rundown/shoe-rotation-two-pairs) covers how to pair them.

guides.title: Nike Pegasus Alternatives: Similar Daily Trainers by Price and Feel
guides.excerpt: The Saucony Ride 19 matches the Pegasus 42 on price at $145 and weighs 0.5 oz less. The Winflo 12 is the cheaper Nike option at $110.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** The Saucony Ride 19 is the closest alternative to the Nike Pegasus 42: $145, 9.3 oz and an 8 mm drop. For less money, the Nike Winflo 12 is $110.

## The Pegasus 42 is the benchmark

The [Pegasus 42](/shoes/nike-pegasus-42) is $145, 9.8 oz, with a 37 mm stack and a 10 mm drop. It is a durable, moderately cushioned trainer with an accommodating fit. Our data lists its weaknesses as an incremental update and middle-of-the-pack weight.

Every shoe below is a neutral daily trainer within $5 of it, unless noted.

## The Saucony Ride 19 is the closest match

The [Ride 19](/shoes/saucony-ride-19) is $145 and 9.3 oz with a 35 mm stack and an 8 mm drop. It is the same kind of shoe: balanced cushion, durable outsole and upper, one pair for most of a training week.

It is wrong for runners who like the Pegasus's 10 mm drop and want it kept.

## Other neutral trainers that fit the same job

- [Mizuno Wave Rider 30](/shoes/mizuno-wave-rider-30): $145, 9.8 oz, 38 mm stack, 12 mm drop. Structured and built to last, with a firmer feel.
- [ASICS Gel-Cumulus 28](/shoes/asics-gel-cumulus-28): $145, 9.2 oz, 38 mm stack, 8 mm drop. Light for its cushion.
- Brooks Ghost 18: $150, 9.8 oz, 36 mm stack, 12 mm drop. The safest fit for most feet.
- [Puma Velocity Nitro 5](/shoes/puma-velocity-nitro-5): $140, 8.1 oz, 37 mm stack, 8 mm drop. The lightest of the group, with good wet grip.
- New Balance Fresh Foam X 880 v15: $140, 10.4 oz, 36 mm stack, 8 mm drop. Heavier, with width options.

## Spend less with the Winflo 12 or the last model

The [Winflo 12](/shoes/nike-winflo-12) is $110 and 9.7 oz with a 36 mm stack and a 10 mm drop, the same drop as the Pegasus. It is firmer than Nike's premium foams and is built for easy running, not workouts.

The Pegasus 41 is listed at $140 and 9.9 oz. Our [Pegasus 42 vs 41 guide](/rundown/nike-pegasus-42-vs-41) covers what changed between them.

## Who should skip all of these

Runners who want more cushion should look at the max-cushion tier instead, such as the Nike Vomero 18 at $150 and 46 mm. Runners who want a lighter shoe for workouts should read our [lightweight trainers guide](/rundown/lightweight-trainers-for-faster-days).

guides.title: Brooks vs Hoka vs ASICS: How the Big Three Running Shoe Brands Differ
guides.excerpt: Brooks runs the highest drop and the firmest ride, Hoka the tallest stack, and ASICS sits between them at 8 mm drop. Pick the brand by the ride you want, not the logo.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Brooks is the safe, firmer choice with a 10 to 12 mm drop. Hoka is the tallest and softest, ASICS is the middle option at 8 mm drop, and each brand's flagship daily trainer costs $145 to $150.

## The three flagships cost the same and weigh within 0.6 oz

Each brand has one daily trainer that most runners buy first. Numbers are from our shoe data, men's sizes.

- [Brooks Ghost 18](/shoes/brooks-ghost-18): $150, 9.8 oz, 36 mm stack, 12 mm drop
- [Hoka Clifton 11](/shoes/hoka-clifton-11): $150, 9.7 oz, 42 mm stack, 8 mm drop
- [ASICS Gel-Cumulus 28](/shoes/asics-gel-cumulus-28): $145, 9.2 oz, 38 mm stack, 8 mm drop

Price and weight do not separate them. Stack and drop do.

## Brooks is the firmest and highest drop

The Ghost 18 has the shortest stack of the three and a 12 mm drop. Our data lists it as dependable, durable and a fit for most feet, with wide sizes available. Its weakness is little energy return.

The plush Brooks is the Glycerin 23 at $165 and 10.1 oz, still at a 10 mm drop. Stability runners get the Adrenaline GTS 26 at $155.

## Hoka is the tallest and softest

The Clifton 11 stands 42 mm tall with a rocker shape, and the Bondi 9 goes to 43 mm at $170 and 10.6 oz. Hoka drops are lower: 8 mm on the Clifton and 5 mm on the Bondi.

The cost is versatility. Both are heavy and sluggish above easy pace. The lighter Hoka is the [Mach 7](/shoes/hoka-mach-7) at $145 and 8.3 oz, a daily trainer that handles tempo runs.

## ASICS sits in the middle and runs 8 mm across the range

The Cumulus 28, the [Novablast 6](/shoes/asics-novablast-6) and the Gel-Nimbus 29 all have an 8 mm drop. That makes switching between ASICS models easy on the calves.

- Cumulus 28: the plain daily trainer, light for its cushion
- Novablast 6: $150, 9.0 oz, 41 mm stack, the bouncy one
- Nimbus 29: $170, 9.8 oz, 43 mm stack, the plush one

## Pick by drop and softness

Buy Brooks if you want a firm, protective trainer and run fine at 10 to 12 mm drop. Buy Hoka if softness and standing comfort matter most. Buy ASICS if you want a lighter shoe or plan to own more than one model.

Brooks is wrong for runners who want a soft, tall ride. Hoka is wrong for anyone who wants one shoe that also does workouts. ASICS is wrong for runners who want a roomy toe box, since most of its range is standard width.

Our [heel drop guide](/rundown/heel-drop-explained-4mm-vs-10mm) covers switching between drops, and the [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector) filters all three brands by cushion and fit.

guides.title: 5K and 10K Race Shoes: Light and Firm Beats Plated and Tall
guides.excerpt: For a 5K or 10K, buy a light, firm shoe under 7 oz. The ASICS Hyper Speed 6 is $95 and 6.6 oz, and it's the one to start with.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Buy a light, firm racing flat for a 5K or 10K. The ASICS Hyper Speed 6 is $95 and 6.6 oz, and our data calls it the cheapest true speed shoe in its lineup.

## Short races need weight savings, not stack

A 5K or 10K is over before cushion matters, so the shoes built for it are low and light. All five below weigh 7.1 oz or less and have a stack of 33 mm or lower. Their usual trade is a firm ride that gets harsh past 10K, which is why our notes flag most of them as wrong for longer races.

## Five options from our data

- [ASICS Hyper Speed 6](/shoes/asics-hyper-speed-6): $95, 6.6 oz, 33 mm, 5 mm drop. "Light, flexible, natural-feeling", with "modest cushioning and bounce".
- [Adidas Adizero Adios 9](/shoes/adidas-adizero-adios-9): $130, 7.1 oz, 27 mm, 8 mm. "Nimble, close-to-the-ground ride" and a durable Continental rubber outsole.
- [Topo Athletic Cyclone 3](/shoes/topo-athletic-cyclone-3): $150, 6.9 oz, 28 mm, 5 mm. Roomy toe box, but "limited wet-surface traction".
- [Nike Streakfly 2](/shoes/nike-streakfly-2): $170, 6.2 oz, 32 mm, 6 mm. A midfoot plate and the lightest of the five, with "too little cushion for long races".
- [Adidas Adizero Takumi Sen 11](/shoes/adidas-adizero-takumi-sen-11): $180, 6.5 oz, 33 mm, 6 mm. Grippy outsole, narrow racing fit, "too firm and low for most runners over 10K".

## The Hyper Speed 6 is the default

It costs $35 less than the next cheapest option and is "durable enough to train in", so it covers intervals as well as race day. Plateless shoes also take less getting used to than a carbon plate.

Pick the Takumi Sen 11 instead if you land on your midfoot or forefoot and want the most aggressive fit. Pick the Cyclone 3 if other racing flats pinch your toes and the race will be dry.

## Who a racing flat is wrong for

- Runners whose 10K takes over an hour. The firm ride gets harder to tolerate the longer you're on it, so a lightweight trainer is the safer fit.
- Anyone racing a half marathon or longer. The [half marathon shoe guide](/rundown/half-marathon-shoes-what-to-wear-on-race-day) covers that.
- Runners who want one shoe for everything. The Saucony Endorphin Speed 6 is $175 and 8.2 oz, with a 38 mm stack.

Filter by price on the [speed work shoes under $120](/shoes/best/speed-work-shoes-under-120) list, or use the [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector).

guides.title: Running Shoes for Rain: Grip on Wet Roads Matters Most
guides.excerpt: Buy for outsole grip, not the upper. The Puma Velocity Nitro 5 is $140 and 8.1 oz, and our notes say it has great grip in the wet.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Buy a shoe with proven wet-road grip. The Puma Velocity Nitro 5 is $140 and 8.1 oz, and our notes list "great grip in the wet".

## Wet grip is a rubber question

Our data records traction notes shoe by shoe, and the difference in the wet is clear. Three shoes are flagged as good in the wet, and four are flagged as weak. Check this before you buy, because wet roads are where weak rubber shows.

## Three shoes our notes flag as good in the wet

- [Puma Velocity Nitro 5](/shoes/puma-velocity-nitro-5): $140, 8.1 oz, 37 mm, 8 mm drop. "Great grip in the wet" and "light, versatile trainer".
- [New Balance Ellipse](/shoes/new-balance-ellipse): $145, 9.6 oz, 38 mm, 8 mm. "Good wet-road traction".
- [Craft Nordlite Tempo](/shoes/craft-nordlite-tempo): $180, 9.5 oz, 40 mm, 6 mm. "Excellent wet-road grip", with Vittoria-designed rubber. The fit runs narrow and slightly small.

## The Velocity Nitro 5 is the default

It is the lightest and cheapest of the three, and its 37 mm stack suits easy and steady runs. The New Balance Ellipse is \$5 more with a 38 mm stack and is heavier at 9.6 oz. The Nordlite Tempo costs $40 more and is heavier, so pick it only for the extra stack or its tempo-ready ride.

## Four shoes to skip on wet roads

- ASICS Gel-Cumulus 26: "outsole grip average in wet".
- Reebok Floatzig 2: "wet traction issues from open Zig outsole".
- Salomon Aero Blaze 3: "wet grip is mediocre in the forefoot".
- Topo Athletic Cyclone 3: "limited wet-surface traction".

These are fine on dry roads, and the Cumulus 26 and Floatzig 2 are budget-friendly at \$140 and \$120. The Salomon Aero Blaze 3 is \$140 and 7.9 oz, and the Cyclone 3 is a light speed shoe at \$150. If you already own one, run it on the [treadmill](/rundown/treadmill-running-shoes) or save it for sunny days.

## Who this is wrong for

Runners who only run in rain a few times a year. Keep your current daily trainer, since the difference only shows on wet pavement. Our data lists no waterproof shoe, so wet feet are likely in any of these.

Filter by price and fit with the [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector).

guides.title: Treadmill Running Shoes: Do You Need a Different Pair?
guides.excerpt: No. Wear your regular daily trainer on a treadmill. Shoes with weak wet grip, like the ASICS Gel-Cumulus 26, lose nothing indoors.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** You don't need a treadmill-specific shoe. Wear your regular daily trainer, and save any shoe with weak wet grip for the belt, where grip never gets tested by rain.

## Our data has no treadmill category

We don't list a shoe as built for treadmills, and no gear review in our data claims one runs better on a belt. The only shoe whose notes mention treadmill miles is the [Hoka Kawana 2](/shoes/hoka-kawana-2). It is described as a run-to-gym crossover, a firmer, flatter, more stable shoe for treadmill miles, lifting and errands. It is $140, 10.4 oz, 36 mm, 5 mm drop.

## Indoors is the place for shoes that slip in the rain

Our notes flag several shoes for weak wet grip. A belt is dry, so that weakness costs you nothing there:

- ASICS Gel-Cumulus 26: $140, 9.0 oz, 38.5 mm. "Outsole grip average in wet".
- [Reebok Floatzig 2](/shoes/reebok-floatzig-2): $120, 10.3 oz, 33 mm. "Wet traction issues from open Zig outsole", and it is "great for easy and recovery miles".
- Topo Athletic Cyclone 3: $150, 6.9 oz, 28 mm. "Limited wet-surface traction", and a good light shoe for treadmill intervals.

Using them indoors also saves your outdoor shoes for the road. It also means the grip flaw that rules them out for rain, covered in the [rain shoes guide](/rundown/running-shoes-for-rain), never comes up. A belt does not get wet, so only the cushion and weight of the shoe matter.

## The Floatzig 2 is the cheap treadmill pair

At $120 it is the cheapest of the three, and its listed use is easy miles. A second pair kept at the gym also means no shoe change in the car.

Skip it if your treadmill runs are fast. For those, the Cyclone 3 is the lighter pick and the [lightweight trainers guide](/rundown/lightweight-trainers-for-faster-days) has more.

## Who this is wrong for

- Runners with one pair. Wear your daily trainer, such as the [Brooks Ghost 18](/shoes/brooks-ghost-18) at $150 and 9.8 oz.
- Runners who also lift. The Kawana 2 is the one to look at.
- Anyone setting a treadmill pace. Read the [1% incline guide](/rundown/treadmill-pace-vs-outdoor-pace-1-percent-incline) first; shoes don't change that number.

Compare more in the [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector).

guides.title: Winter Running Shoes for Cold Roads: What to Look For
guides.excerpt: Buy a shoe with proven wet grip and avoid foams that firm up in the cold. The Puma Velocity Nitro 5 is $140, and our data flags the $80 New Balance 680 v8 as stiffening.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** For cold roads, buy a shoe with proven wet grip, since winter is wet. The Puma Velocity Nitro 5 is $140 and 8.1 oz, with "great grip in the wet".

## Our data flags one shoe for cold foam

The [New Balance Fresh Foam 680 v8](/shoes/new-balance-fresh-foam-680-v8) is $80, 9.5 oz, 35 mm. Our notes say the midsole "firms up noticeably in cold weather". It is a sensible first running shoe, so it still fits a budget in mild weather.

The Ellipse and Velocity Nitro 5 notes list no cold-weather issue, though that is a gap in our notes and not a test result. We have not tested cold foam shoe by shoe, so the data flags this one only. If a shoe feels hard on a cold morning, give it the first mile to settle.

## Pick grip first

Rain and slush matter more than temperature for most winter runs, and wet pavement is where weak rubber slips. Check the outsole notes before the foam notes. Shoes our notes list as good in the wet:

- [Puma Velocity Nitro 5](/shoes/puma-velocity-nitro-5): $140, 8.1 oz, 37 mm.
- [New Balance Ellipse](/shoes/new-balance-ellipse): $145, 9.6 oz, 38 mm.
- Craft Nordlite Tempo: $180, 9.5 oz, 40 mm, with "excellent wet-road grip". The fit runs narrow and slightly small, so it suits runners who already know they fit Craft.

The [rain shoes guide](/rundown/running-shoes-for-rain) lists four to skip.

## The Ellipse is the pick for slow winter miles

It costs $5 more than the Velocity Nitro 5 and has a taller 38 mm stack. At 9.6 oz it is heavier, which does not matter at easy pace. Choose the Velocity Nitro 5 if you do faster runs in the cold.

## Who this is wrong for

- Runners on snow or ice. Our data lists no shoe with snow or ice traction, and these are road shoes.
- Anyone with one good daily pair. Keep it, and add a [second pair for rotation](/rundown/shoe-rotation-two-pairs) only if wet days wear it out.
- Runners shopping on price alone. Check the [last year's model guide](/rundown/last-years-running-shoe-model-what-changes) for savings.

Compare more in the [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector).

guides.title: Half Marathon Shoes: What to Wear on Race Day
guides.excerpt: The ASICS Magic Speed 5 at $160 is the half marathon pick: a full carbon plate, 8.0 oz and a tough build. Wear your trainer if you haven't practiced in a plated shoe, and skip anything under 30 mm of stack.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Race a half marathon in the ASICS Magic Speed 5: $160, 8.0 oz, a full carbon plate and a 39 mm stack. Your trainer is the better choice if you haven't run long in a plated shoe.

## A half sits between a trainer and a super shoe

A half marathon is long enough that cushion matters and short enough that a lighter shoe helps. Our data lists the Magic Speed 5 as "strong plated performance per dollar" and "lighter than most trainers".

Its cons are "less bouncy than flagship racers" and a narrow-ish performance fit.

## Four options from our data

- [ASICS Magic Speed 5](/shoes/asics-magic-speed-5): $160, 8.0 oz, 39 mm, 8 mm drop. Tough enough for repeated tempo sessions.
- [New Balance FuelCell Rebel v5](/shoes/new-balance-fuelcell-rebel-v5): $140, 7.8 oz, 35 mm, 6 mm drop. No plate, a "very light" ride, and average outsole durability.
- [Hoka Rocket X 3](/shoes/hoka-rocket-x-3): $250, 7.4 oz, 40 mm. Our notes call it a "strong half-to-full marathon pick" with an unusually stable ride.
- [Saucony Endorphin Speed 6](/shoes/saucony-endorphin-speed-6): $175, 8.2 oz. A nylon plate, and it trains well too.

## The Magic Speed 5 is the default

It is the cheapest full carbon plate in this list. It's also $15 under the Endorphin Speed 6, which is the better pick if you want a forgiving nylon plate. Our [Speed 6 versus Pro 5 guide](/rundown/saucony-endorphin-speed-6-vs-pro-5) compares the two Saucony plates.

## What to skip

- Shoes under about 30 mm of stack for a half. The Adidas Adizero Adios 9 is 27 mm and our data says its cushion is minimal for marathon distance.
- A shoe you haven't run in. Do at least two tempo runs or one long run in the shoe first.
- A new shoe in the week before the race. Pick it a month out.

## Who this is wrong for

- Runners new to the distance. A daily trainer is the safer pick, and the [daily trainer guide](/rundown/what-is-a-daily-trainer) explains why.
- Runners on a tight budget. The $95 ASICS Hyper Speed 6 is better at 5K and 10K, and our data says it isn't a marathon shoe for most.
- Runners with a $250 budget and a goal time. Plenty of super shoes are on the race-day list.

Fuel plans for the distance are in the [half marathon gel guide](/rundown/how-many-gels-for-a-half-marathon).

guides.title: Marathon Race Shoe: Plated, Unplated, or Your Daily Trainer?
guides.excerpt: For most marathoners the plated Saucony Endorphin Speed 6 at $175 is the sensible race shoe. Your trainer is fine if you have no plated long runs yet, and a $250 super shoe is for chasing a time.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Race the marathon in a plated shoe once you've run two long runs in it, such as the $175 Saucony Endorphin Speed 6. Without that practice, wear your daily trainer.

## What a plate was measured to do

Hoogkamer and colleagues (2018, Sports Medicine) put 18 male runners on a treadmill in a Nike prototype and two other marathon shoes. Energetic cost was about 4% lower in the prototype. Each runner had run a 10K in under 31 minutes, so the figure is for very fast men.

Our [carbon plate guide](/rundown/carbon-plate-shoes-for-non-elite-runners) covers what that means at slower paces. We don't quote a saving for them.

## Three choices from our data

- Your trainer. The Nike Zoom Fly 6 is a carbon super trainer at $170, 9.4 oz and 42 mm. It is "noticeably heavier than race-day supershoes".
- Plated, mid-price. The [Endorphin Speed 6](/shoes/saucony-endorphin-speed-6) has a nylon plate, 38 mm stack and 8 mm drop. Our data lists it as durable enough for regular training and says it fits slightly short.
- Super shoe. The [Vaporfly 4](/shoes/nike-vaporfly-4) is $260 and 6.0 oz. The Adidas Adizero Adios Pro 5 is $250 and 7.6 oz, built for full-effort half marathons and marathons.

## The Endorphin Speed 6 is the default

It costs $75 to $85 less than the super shoes and gives up 1.6 oz to 2.2 oz. It is also firm enough to train in, so the two practice long runs are cheap to do.

Buy the Zoom Fly 6 instead if you want a single plated shoe for long runs and race day. The [super trainers guide](/rundown/super-trainers-explained) covers that category.

## Break it in before race day

Run at least two long runs in the shoe, one of them with a stretch at goal pace. Check for hot spots and toe room after mile 15, not mile 3. Taper runs don't count, because tired legs are what you are testing.

Plan fueling too: the [marathon gel guide](/rundown/how-many-gels-for-a-marathon) has the numbers.

## Who this advice is wrong for

- Wide feet. The Vaporfly 4 is narrow, and the Endorphin Speed 6 is standard width.
- First-time marathoners running to finish. Your trainer is the safest pick, as the [first racing shoe guide](/rundown/how-to-choose-your-first-racing-shoe) explains.
- Runners with a time goal who want the lightest option. Compare the [Vaporfly 4 and Alphafly 4](/rundown/nike-vaporfly-4-vs-alphafly-4).

guides.title: Running Shoes for Flat Feet: What You Need and What You Can Skip
guides.excerpt: Flat feet don't require a stability shoe. The ASICS GT-1000 15 at $100 is the supported pick if you want one, and a neutral trainer is fine if it feels better.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Flat feet don't require a stability shoe. If you want support, the ASICS GT-1000 15 is $100 and 9.4 oz, and a neutral trainer is fine if it feels better.

## Flat feet didn't predict injuries in the main study

In 2014 Nielsen and colleagues followed 927 novice runners for a year in the same neutral shoe (British Journal of Sports Medicine). Runners with pronated feet did not have a significantly higher injury risk than runners with neutral feet after 250 km. It is one study of beginners in one shoe, so it says nothing about what a stability shoe does for a particular person.

Nigg and colleagues (2015, same journal) proposed that runners pick shoes through a "comfort filter", meaning the shoe that feels best is a reasonable guide. That is a proposal, not a settled result.

## The GT-1000 15 is the default

The [ASICS GT-1000 15](/shoes/asics-gt-1000-15) is $100, 9.4 oz, with a 35 mm stack and 8 mm drop. Our data calls it "strong value for supported miles" and lists a basic foam package as its limit. It is the cheapest current stability trainer in the data, so it costs little to find out whether you like the feel.

## Other supported options from our data

- [Saucony Omni 22](/shoes/saucony-omni-22): $140, 10.1 oz. Our notes call it a pick for "overpronators and flat-footed runners who want structure", with a dull ride and a long break-in.
- [Brooks Adrenaline GTS 26](/shoes/brooks-adrenaline-gts-26): $155, 10.8 oz, 10 mm drop. Wide sizing options.
- [Saucony Guide 19](/shoes/saucony-guide-19): $145, 9.4 oz, 6 mm drop. Stable and planted, uninspiring for speed work.
- [Saucony Echelon 11](/shoes/saucony-echelon-11): $155, 11.5 oz. Roomy, and our data says it fits custom orthotics.

## Test it before you commit

Jog a few minutes in a supportive shoe and a neutral one with similar cushion. Keep the one you notice least. The [stability versus neutral guide](/rundown/stability-shoes-vs-neutral-do-you-need-support) covers the test in more detail.

If you switch types, run one or two easy runs in the new pair before a long run. The [shoe selector](/tools/shoe-selector) can filter by stability.

## Who this is wrong for

- Runners who use prescribed orthotics. Check the fit with them in the shoe, and start with the Echelon 11.
- Heavier runners who want a wider base. The [heavier runners guide](/rundown/running-shoes-for-heavier-runners) fits better.
- Anyone with foot pain. See a doctor or physical therapist, because a shoe won't treat it.

guides.title: Running Shoes for High Arches: Pick Cushion and Comfort First
guides.excerpt: High arches don't need a special shoe type. The Hoka Clifton 11 at $150 and 42 mm is a soft default, and the Skechers Aero Burst at $130 is the cheaper cushioned option.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** High arches don't call for a special shoe. Pick a cushioned neutral trainer that feels comfortable, such as the Hoka Clifton 11 at $150, 9.7 oz and 42 mm.

## No study we can name ties arch height to a shoe type

Our shoe data has no arch field, so we don't claim to match shoes to arch height. The study we can cite is Nielsen and colleagues (2014, British Journal of Sports Medicine): 927 novice runners in one neutral shoe, followed for a year. Runners with supinated feet, the high-arch posture, had no significant difference in injury risk from neutral feet after 250 km.

It is one study of beginners. It supports choosing by comfort, which Nigg and colleagues (2015, same journal) proposed as a "comfort filter".

## Start with a neutral trainer with plenty of cushion

Cushion is the one spec you can check in our data. These are all neutral, maximum-cushion trainers:

- [Hoka Clifton 11](/shoes/hoka-clifton-11): $150, 9.7 oz, 42 mm, 8 mm drop. "Familiar plush Clifton ride".
- [Brooks Glycerin 23](/shoes/brooks-glycerin-23): $165, 10.1 oz, 38 mm, 10 mm drop. "Plush, premium ride".
- [ASICS Gel-Nimbus 29](/shoes/asics-gel-nimbus-29): $170, 9.8 oz, 43 mm, 8 mm drop. Too soft for fast workouts.
- [Skechers Aero Burst](/shoes/skechers-aero-burst): $130, 9.0 oz, 38 mm, 6 mm drop. Soft and cheap, with an upper that runs warm.

## The Clifton 11 is the default

It is $15 under the Glycerin 23 and lighter. Our data lists "smooth rockered transitions" as a strength and says it isn't versatile for faster paces.

Buy the Aero Burst instead if $130 is the ceiling. Our data lists limited run-specialty distribution, so check the return policy before you order.

## Check three things on day one

- Toe room. Your longest toe should have a thumb's width in front of it.
- Heel hold. The heel shouldn't lift on a jog.
- Midfoot pressure. A tight spot over the top of the foot means the lacing or the shoe is wrong.

The [sizing guide](/rundown/running-shoe-sizing-half-size-up) explains the half size up.

## Who this is wrong for

- Runners who like ground feel. A tall, soft stack mutes it, and the [max cushion guide](/rundown/max-cushion-running-shoes-who-they-help) covers the trade.
- Runners who feel unsteady in soft shoes. Try a mild stability trainer such as the [Brooks Ghost Max 4](/shoes/brooks-ghost-max-4).
- Anyone with foot pain. See a doctor or physical therapist.

The [shoe selector](/tools/shoe-selector) filters by cushion.

guides.title: Recovery Run Shoes: Pick Soft and Stable, Skip Anything Built for Speed
guides.excerpt: A recovery shoe is soft and stable and doesn't need to be light. The Saucony Triumph 24 at $170 and 37 mm is the pick, and the ASICS Gel-Excite 11 at $90 is the cheap one.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Pick a soft, stable shoe with a 37 mm or taller stack for recovery days. The Saucony Triumph 24 is $170 and 9.7 oz, and our data lists it as "excellent for long easy miles".

## Recovery days need cushion, not speed

Recovery runs are short and easy, so weight and pop don't matter. Our data lists the shoes built for it as "too soft and tall for fast workouts", which is the point. A dedicated pair also keeps your fast shoes for fast days, as the [rotation guide](/rundown/shoe-rotation-two-pairs) explains.

## Five soft options from our data

- [Saucony Triumph 24](/shoes/saucony-triumph-24): $170, 9.7 oz, 37 mm, 10 mm drop. "Plush, energetic PEBA cushioning".
- [Brooks Ghost Max 4](/shoes/brooks-ghost-max-4): $160, 10.3 oz, 39 mm, 6 mm. "Maximum protection for easy miles" with a stable base.
- ASICS Gel-Nimbus 29: $170, 9.8 oz, 43 mm, 8 mm. Plush, and lighter than the Nimbus 28.
- Hoka Bondi 9: $170, 10.6 oz, 43 mm, 5 mm. "Very protective for recovery days", and sluggish above easy pace.
- Saucony Procyon Max: $120, 10.7 oz, 38 mm, 6 mm. The budget pick, with "lots of cushion for $120".

## The Triumph 24 is the default

It is the lightest of the five at 9.7 oz and listed for recovery runs. Its limit is price: our data calls it expensive and too soft for fast workouts.

Buy the Procyon Max instead if you want a second pair for $50 less. It is heavier at 10.7 oz and "not lively at faster paces", which does not matter on a recovery day.

## The Gel-Excite 11 is the cheapest at $90

The [ASICS Gel-Excite 11](/shoes/asics-gel-excite-11) is $90, 10.2 oz, 38 mm, and our notes say it is "comfortable for walking/easy miles". It also lists "heavy and basic foam" and "not built for serious mileage", so treat it as a short-run shoe.

## Who this advice is wrong for

- Runners who run 3 days a week. One daily trainer is enough, so start with the [daily trainer guide](/rundown/what-is-a-daily-trainer).
- Forefoot strikers who dislike a 10 mm drop. The Triumph 24 is 10 mm, and our Triumph 23 notes say the drop "won't suit forefoot strikers". The Ghost Max 4 at 6 mm is the alternative.
- Heavier runners who want more support. The [heavier runners guide](/rundown/running-shoes-for-heavier-runners) fits them better.

Filter for soft shoes in the [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector) or the [max cushion recovery list](/shoes/best/max-cushion-recovery-shoes).

guides.title: Lightweight Running Shoes for Faster Days: Five Trainers Under 8.5 oz
guides.excerpt: The Hoka Mach 7 at $145 and 8.3 oz is the default light trainer for tempo days. The Saucony Kinvara 16 at 7.0 oz is lighter, but our data calls it firm over long runs.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Buy the Hoka Mach 7 ($145, 8.3 oz, 37 mm stack, 5 mm drop) as the light shoe for tempo runs and intervals. It also works for easy miles, so it can be your only trainer.

## The Mach 7 is the default

The [Hoka Mach 7](/shoes/hoka-mach-7) is built for easy pace through tempo, with a 37 mm stack that protects longer efforts. Our notes list it as "versatile from easy pace to tempo" and "light for a full daily trainer".

Its limit: our data says it is not for max-cushion lovers, so it is a poor recovery shoe. The Mach 6 at $140 and 8.2 oz had thin outsole rubber, and the Mach 7 adds slightly improved coverage.

## Four others with different trade-offs

- [Saucony Kinvara 16](/shoes/saucony-kinvara-16): $130, 7.0 oz, 29 mm, 4 mm drop. The lightest here, but "low energy return from dated foam" and a narrow fit.
- [New Balance FuelCell Rebel v5](/shoes/new-balance-fuelcell-rebel-v5): $140, 7.8 oz, 35 mm, 6 mm. "Very light with lively bounce", and rated down for average outsole durability.
- Brooks Launch 11: $120, 7.7 oz, 34 mm, 8 mm. The budget pick, with "basic firm foam" and sparse cushioning for long runs.
- Skechers Aero Spark: $120, 7.6 oz, 33 mm, 6 mm. "Light and lively for the price", with thin outsole rubber.

## Pick by what you do on the fast day

For 400 m to mile repeats, the lighter and lower shoes fit: the Kinvara 16 at 29 mm or the Aero Spark at 33 mm. For a 40 to 60 minute tempo, the Mach 7 at 37 mm or the Rebel v5 at 35 mm give more foam under you.

Race-day pace is a separate question. Plated shoes are covered in the [carbon plate guide](/rundown/carbon-plate-shoes-for-non-elite-runners).

## Light shoes wear faster

Several of the shoes above list thin outsole rubber or average durability in our data. Expect fewer miles from them than from a heavier daily trainer. The signs to watch are in our [shoe lifespan guide](/rundown/how-long-do-running-shoes-last).

## Who this advice is wrong for

- Runners who need stability. These five are neutral and light.
- Heavier runners. Our data says the lightweight Aero Blaze 3 has a "midsole that compresses under heavier runners".
- Anyone doing all their runs at easy pace. A [daily trainer](/rundown/what-is-a-daily-trainer) is the better single shoe.

Sort by weight and price in the [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector), or use the [lightweight speed work list](/shoes/best/lightweight-speed-work-shoes).

guides.title: Last Year's Running Shoe Model: What Changes and When to Buy It
guides.excerpt: Between versions our data shows the same stack and drop and weight shifts of 0.1 oz. Buy last year's model whenever it costs less, unless the update changed the foam.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Buy last year's model if it's cheaper. Across 10 version updates in our data, weight moved 0.1 oz or less and drop never changed.

## Most updates are small

We compared the latest version with the one before it for daily trainers with two generations in our data:

- [Brooks Ghost 17](/shoes/brooks-ghost-17) to [Ghost 18](/shoes/brooks-ghost-18): $150 both, 9.8 oz both, 36 mm stack, 12 mm drop.
- [Hoka Clifton 10](/shoes/hoka-clifton-10) to [Clifton 11](/shoes/hoka-clifton-11): $150 both, 9.8 oz to 9.7 oz, 42 mm, 8 mm.
- ASICS Gel-Cumulus 27 to Cumulus 28: $145 both, 9.3 oz to 9.2 oz, 38 mm, 8 mm.
- Saucony Triumph 23 to Triumph 24: $170 both, 9.8 oz to 9.7 oz, 37 mm, 10 mm.
- ASICS Gel-Nimbus 27 to Nimbus 28: $165 both, 10.7 oz to 10.6 oz, 43 mm, 8 mm.

The exceptions are price rises: the Hoka Mach 6 at $140 became the [Mach 7](/shoes/hoka-mach-7) at $145, and the Ghost 16 at $140 became the Ghost 17 at $150.

## Our notes call several updates modest

The same shoes carry blunt notes. The Pegasus 42 is an "incremental update over the 41", the Glycerin 23 a "small update if you own the 22", and the Ghost Max 4 a "modest update over the Max 3". Our full write-up of one case is in the [Pegasus 42 vs 41 guide](/rundown/nike-pegasus-42-vs-41).

## Buy the old version when it costs less

Our data lists launch prices and does not track sales, so check the retailer's price for both versions. If last year's pair is under the new list price, buy it. A $20 gap on a $150 shoe is about 13 percent.

Check the release date in our shoe data too. The next version often lands about a year after the last, so a shoe released more than 11 months ago is likely due for a replacement.

## Pay for the new one when the foam changed

Some updates swap the midsole, and then weight and price hide the real difference. Our Kinvara 16 note says "low energy return from dated foam", which tells you the foam did not move on. Read the pros and cons on the new shoe's page. If the headline pro is a new foam, the update is worth paying for.

## Who this advice is wrong for

- Runners who wore the old version and liked it. Buy a second pair of it now, before stock disappears.
- Anyone with a fit problem in the old version that the update fixed. Our Arahi 9 note says "wider, roomier forefoot fit" over the Arahi 8.
- Runners with a race coming up. Do not change shoes inside two weeks of it.

Filter by price, drop and cushion in the [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector) before comparing versions.

guides.title: Zero Drop Running Shoes: How to Switch Without Wrecking Your Calves
guides.excerpt: Switch to zero drop over 6 to 8 weeks, starting with one easy run a week in a cushioned pair like the Altra Torin 9 at $150. Skip it if your calves or Achilles already complain.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Spend 6 to 8 weeks moving into zero drop, one easy run a week at first. Start in a cushioned shoe like the Altra Torin 9 ($150, 10.1 oz, 30 mm stack), not a thin one.

## Zero drop moves work to your calves

In a zero-drop shoe the heel and forefoot sit at the same height. Most trainers sit 8 to 12 mm higher at the heel, so the calf and Achilles stretch further on every step. Our data flags the same cost on several models: the Altra Escalante 4 lists "zero drop requires calf adaptation" and the Paradigm 8 says "zero drop needs a calf transition".

The research on drop and injury is thin, as the [heel drop guide](/rundown/heel-drop-explained-4mm-vs-10mm) covers. Treat the ramp below as caution, not a proven protocol.

## Start in a cushioned zero-drop shoe

A thin shoe adds two changes at once: less drop and less foam. These are the zero-drop shoes in our data worth starting in:

- [Altra Torin 9](/shoes/altra-torin-9): $150, 10.1 oz, 30 mm. Our notes call it an "easy transition shoe into zero drop".
- [Topo Magnifly 5](/shoes/topo-athletic-magnifly-5): $140, 9.6 oz, 30 mm. Cushioned, with a wide toe box.
- [Altra Escalante 5](/shoes/altra-escalante-5): $130, 9.2 oz, 24 mm. Thin, "too thin for high mileage", so a later purchase.

## Ramp over 6 to 8 weeks

- Weeks 1 and 2: one easy run a week of 20 to 30 minutes in the zero-drop pair. Everything else stays in your old shoes.
- Weeks 3 and 4: two easy runs a week in them, still under 45 minutes.
- Weeks 5 and 6: add one longer easy run, and keep speed work in your old shoes.
- Weeks 7 and 8: most easy miles in the new pair if your calves feel normal the next morning.

Repeat a step if tightness hasn't faded by the next run. If calf or Achilles pain lingers, see a doctor or physical therapist.

## Try 4 mm first if the jump looks big

Runners coming from 10 or 12 mm shoes can step down in two stages. The [Altra Experience Flow 3](/shoes/altra-experience-flow-3) is $145, 9.0 oz, 32 mm with a 4 mm drop and the same wide toe box. Our [low-drop shoe list](/shoes/best/low-drop-running-shoes) has more.

## Who should skip zero drop

- Runners with calves or Achilles tendons that already flare up in current shoes.
- Anyone training for a race inside 8 weeks. Change shoes after the race, not before.
- Runners who want one shoe for racing. The zero-drop [Altra Vanish Pulse](/shoes/altra-vanish-pulse) is 6.9 oz with a 22 mm stack, and our data limits it to shorter efforts.

The [Shoe Finder](/tools/shoe-selector) filters by drop, cushion and toe box together.

guides.title: Running Shoe Sizing: Why Most Runners Go Up Half a Size
guides.excerpt: Leave half to a full thumb's width in front of your longest toe, which usually means a half size up from your street shoe. Try shoes on in the evening with your running socks.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Leave half to a full thumb's width between your longest toe and the end of the shoe. For most runners that is a half size up from their street shoe size.

## The rule is a thumb's width of space

ASICS says to leave half to a full thumb's width between your toes and the end of the shoe, and to go up half a size if you have less. Brooks and REI give the same thumb's width guide. These are brand and retailer guidelines, not trial results.

To check, stand with the shoe laced and press down on the front. Your longest toe is often the second toe, not the big one.

## Feet swell, so try shoes on late

Nike, ASICS and others advise trying shoes on after a run or in the evening, when feet are larger. A shoe that fits at 8 a.m. may be tight at mile 8. Longer runs call for more room than a 5K does.

Try shoes on with the socks you run in. A thick sock can change the size you need by half a size.

## What a good fit feels like

- A snug heel that does not lift as you walk.
- A midfoot that holds without pressure on the top of the foot.
- Room to spread your toes side to side.
- A thumb's width of space in front of the longest toe.

Width matters as much as length. A shoe that is the right length but too narrow needs a wide size, not a bigger number. Our [wide feet guide](/rundown/wide-feet-running-shoes) covers that case.

## Some models need a different size

Sizing varies by model. Our data says the [Endorphin Speed 6](/shoes/saucony-endorphin-speed-6) fits slightly short and suggests going up. The [Brooks Ghost 18](/shoes/brooks-ghost-18) is listed as fitting most feet, with wide sizes available. Check the model page before you order, and use the [shoe selector](/tools/shoe-selector) to narrow the list.

## Who should not size up

Runners who already have room in front of the toes, or whose heel slips, should stay at their size. A bigger shoe will not fix a heel that lifts. If you buy without trying on, our guide to [buying shoes online](/rundown/buy-running-shoes-online-without-a-fitting) covers the check on day one.

guides.title: How to Buy Running Shoes Online Without a Fitting
guides.excerpt: Measure your foot in the evening, buy the size and model you already wear, and check the return policy before ordering. Test the pair indoors on day one.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Buy the model and size you already wear if it worked. For a new shoe, measure your foot in the evening, check the return policy first and test the pair indoors on day one.

## Start from a shoe you know fits

The safest online purchase is the next version of a shoe you already run in. Updates between versions are usually small, as the [Pegasus 42 vs 41](/rundown/nike-pegasus-42-vs-41) comparison shows. Order the same size.

Switching brands carries the risk. Sizing varies between brands, and between models within a brand. Check our model page for notes on fit. The [Endorphin Speed 6](/shoes/saucony-endorphin-speed-6) listing, for example, says it fits slightly short and suggests sizing up.

## Measure in the evening, then check the size chart

Brand guides from ASICS, Brooks and REI all advise trying shoes on later in the day, when feet are larger. Measure the same way:

- Stand on a sheet of paper in the evening with your heel against a wall.
- Mark the end of your longest toe and measure to the wall in millimeters.
- Compare it to the brand's size chart, which lists foot length per size.
- Pick the size with at least half a thumb's width of extra room, as covered in our [sizing guide](/rundown/running-shoe-sizing-half-size-up).

## Read the return policy before the price

A cheap pair you can't return is not cheap if it doesn't fit. Check three things before checkout:

- Whether returns are free.
- How many days you have.
- Whether you can return shoes after you have worn them outside.

Many shops accept only unworn pairs, so wear the shoes indoors on a clean floor for the first test.

## Test on day one, then decide

Put the shoes on in the evening with the socks you run in. Check these:

- A thumb's width of room in front of the longest toe.
- A heel that doesn't lift when you walk fast.
- No pressure on the sides of the foot.

Jog in place or around a room for a few minutes. If anything rubs or pinches, send them back rather than waiting for them to break in.

## Who this is wrong for

Runners with an unusual foot shape, or with wide feet, will do better in a store for the first pair. Our [wide feet guide](/rundown/wide-feet-running-shoes) lists models that run roomy. After that first fit, ordering online works.

guides.title: Super Trainers Explained: Plated Training Shoes and Who Needs One
guides.excerpt: A super trainer is a daily trainer with race-style foam, sometimes with a plate. The Adizero Evo SL at $150 is the cheapest in our data worth a look, and most runners don't need one.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** A super trainer pairs a tall stack of race-style foam with trainer durability. Most runners should stay in a regular daily trainer, and the Adizero Evo SL ($150, 7.9 oz) is the value entry if you want one.

## A super trainer sits between the daily trainer and the racer

The category covers shoes with 39 to 46 mm of stack and soft, high-rebound foam that also hold up to daily mileage. Some have a plate and some don't. They weigh 8 to 10 oz, lighter than most daily trainers, and cost $150 to $200.

Race shoes are lighter and cost more, and their outsoles are not built for a full training block.

## Plated and plateless versions both exist

- [Adidas Adizero Evo SL](/shoes/adidas-adizero-evo-sl): $150, 7.9 oz, 39 mm stack, 6.5 mm drop. No plate. Thin outsole coverage wears faster.
- [ASICS Superblast 3](/shoes/asics-superblast-3): $200, 8.8 oz, 45 mm stack, 8 mm drop. No plate. Our data calls it overkill for short easy runs.
- [Hoka Mach X 3](/shoes/hoka-mach-x-3): $190, 9.3 oz, 44 mm stack, 5 mm drop. Plated, and more stable than most plated trainers.
- [Puma Deviate Nitro 4](/shoes/puma-deviate-nitro-4): $160, 9.2 oz, 39 mm stack, 10 mm drop. Plated, good value for the category.
- [Brooks Hyperion Max 4](/shoes/brooks-hyperion-max-4): $180, 8.2 oz, 36 mm stack, 6 mm drop. Plated, firmer ride.

## A plate is not what makes the shoe

Foam, stack and weight decide most of the ride. Our data describes the Mach X 3 plate as acting more like a stabilizer than a propulsion element. For more on what plates do for slower runners, see [carbon plates for non-elite runners](/rundown/carbon-plate-shoes-for-non-elite-runners).

## Who should buy one

A super trainer makes sense for runners doing three or more runs a week with a weekly long run and tempo work, who want one shoe for all of it. It also suits runners whose goal race is a marathon and who want the race shoe's feel in training without wearing it out.

It is wrong for beginners, who get more from a [regular daily trainer](/rundown/what-is-a-daily-trainer), and for runners on a budget. A $200 shoe on easy 3-mile days is a lot of price for a small gain.

The Evo SL is the pick if price matters. The Superblast 3 is the pick if you want the most cushion.

guides.title: What Is a Daily Trainer Running Shoe and Which One to Pick
guides.excerpt: A daily trainer is a moderately cushioned shoe built to take most of your weekly miles. For most runners one is enough, and the Brooks Ghost 18 at $150 is our default.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** A daily trainer is a durable, moderately cushioned shoe for easy runs and long runs. Most runners need one pair, and ours is the Brooks Ghost 18 ($150, 9.8 oz, 36 mm stack, 12 mm drop).

## A daily trainer is the shoe that takes most of your miles

Shoe makers sort models by job: daily trainer, recovery shoe, speed shoe, race shoe. The daily trainer is the middle one. It has enough foam for a long run, enough rubber to last hundreds of miles and no plate or racing geometry.

In our data, daily trainers sit at 34 to 41 mm of stack and weigh 9 to 10 oz. Anything lighter and firmer is for workouts. Anything with a much taller stack is a recovery or max-cushion shoe.

## One pair covers most runners

If you run three or four times a week at conversational pace, a single daily trainer does the whole job. A second pair starts to pay off at higher mileage, as covered in our [shoe rotation guide](/rundown/shoe-rotation-two-pairs).

These four are the safe picks in our database:

- [Brooks Ghost 18](/shoes/brooks-ghost-18): $150, 9.8 oz, 36 mm stack, 12 mm drop. Firm and dependable.
- [Nike Pegasus 42](/shoes/nike-pegasus-42): $145, 9.8 oz, 37 mm stack, 10 mm drop. Durable, accommodating fit.
- Saucony Ride 19: $145, 9.3 oz, 35 mm stack, 8 mm drop. The lightest of the four.
- ASICS Novablast 6: $150, 9.0 oz, 41 mm stack, 8 mm drop. Bouncier, and less stable.

## Pick by fit, then by feel

The four shoes are close enough that fit decides. A shoe that fits badly will not get worn, and the spec sheet does not change that. Our [guide for beginners](/rundown/best-running-shoes-for-beginners) covers fit in more detail.

After fit, choose on ride. The Ghost 18 is the firmest of the four. The Novablast 6 has the most bounce, and our data lists its platform as not the most stable.

## Who a daily trainer is wrong for

- Runners who race often: a lighter shoe helps on race day. See [how to choose your first racing shoe](/rundown/how-to-choose-your-first-racing-shoe).
- Runners who want maximum softness: the max-cushion models in our [guide](/rundown/max-cushion-running-shoes-who-they-help) have 43 mm or more of stack.
- Runners who need guide rails: see [stability vs neutral](/rundown/stability-shoes-vs-neutral-do-you-need-support).

Use the [shoe selector](/tools/shoe-selector) to filter by your foot and pace.

guides.title: Running Shoes for Heavier Runners: Four Picks With Stable Bases
guides.excerpt: Heavier runners should look for a wide stable base and durable foam. The Brooks Ghost Max 4 at $160 is the default, and Hoka's Gaviota 6 adds support at $175.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Buy a wide-based, durable max cushion trainer. The Brooks Ghost Max 4 is $160 and 10.3 oz, and our data says its stable-neutral base suits heavier runners.

## Look for width and durable foam

Our shoe notes for heavier runners come back to a wide base, durable foam and a sturdy outsole.

Weight does matter. Our data warns that the Salomon Aero Blaze 3 at $140 has a "midsole that compresses under heavier runners". The Mizuno Neo Zen 2 lists "foam durability trails firmer trainers".

## The Ghost Max 4 is the default pick

The [Brooks Ghost Max 4](/shoes/brooks-ghost-max-4) is $160 with a 39 mm stack, 6 mm drop and a rocker. Its limits are weight and pace: 10.3 oz, and our data calls it too heavy for workouts.

Treat it as the easy-day and long-run shoe. Fast days need a lighter pair.

## Other picks with data behind them

- [Saucony Hurricane 25](/shoes/saucony-hurricane-25): $160, 10.7 oz, 38 mm, moderate stability, "durable enough for heavier runners".
- [Hoka Gaviota 6](/shoes/hoka-gaviota-6): $175, 10.9 oz, 39 mm, moderate stability, "great for bigger runners and long easy days".
- Diadora Cellula 2: $185, 10.9 oz, 38 mm, very protective and stable, and it runs short.
- Saucony Procyon Max: $120, 10.7 oz, 38 mm, the budget option with a broad base.

## Choose Hurricane 25 over Ghost Max 4 if you want more guidance

The [Saucony Hurricane 25](/shoes/saucony-hurricane-25) has moderate stability where the Ghost Max 4 is rated mild. Both are $160 and within 0.4 oz of each other. Pick the Hurricane if your ankles roll inward in your current shoes, and the Ghost Max 4 if you want a neutral feel with a wide base.

Skip very soft, tall shoes known for wobble, such as the Novablast 6, whose data lists "not the most stable platform".

## Check for packed-down foam early

Soft foam can compress under more load, as the Aero Blaze 3 note shows. If a shoe feels flat sooner than expected, the signs are in our [shoe lifespan guide](/rundown/how-long-do-running-shoes-last).

## Who this advice is wrong for

- Runners who want a light, fast shoe. Every pick above is over 10 oz, and none fits a tempo day.
- Runners who need a heavy stability shoe. Our [stability and neutral guide](/rundown/stability-shoes-vs-neutral-do-you-need-support) covers who benefits.
- Anyone buying by weight alone. Try shoes on, and filter further with the [shoe selector](/tools/shoe-selector) or the [list for heavy runners](/shoes/best/running-shoes-for-heavy-runners).

guides.title: Running Shoes for Wide Feet: Models With a Roomy Toe Box
guides.excerpt: Our data lists 39 of 339 shoes with a wide or extra-wide toe box, and 16 are Altra. The Altra Torin 9 is the default pick at $150, and the Saucony Echelon 11 is the widest.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Start with the Altra Torin 9 at $150, or the Saucony Echelon 11 at $155 if your feet are very wide. Our data lists only 39 of 339 shoes with a wide or extra-wide toe box.

## Roomy toe boxes are rare

Of 339 shoes in our database, 44 are narrow and 256 are standard. Only 34 are wide and 5 are extra wide.

Altra makes 16 of the 39. Topo Athletic has 7, Brooks 5 and Saucony 4. The rest are Mount to Coast, New Balance, Craft, Hoka and Reebok.

## The Torin 9 is the default pick

The [Altra Torin 9](/shoes/altra-torin-9) is $150 and 10.1 oz with a 30 mm stack and zero drop. Our data calls it the safest recommendation for runners moving into low-drop shoes who still want real cushioning.

Zero drop is the catch. If your calves are used to a 10 mm shoe, read the [heel drop guide](/rundown/heel-drop-explained-4mm-vs-10mm) before buying, or take the Altra Experience Flow 3 at $145 with a 4 mm drop.

## Models by what you need

- Widest fit: [Saucony Echelon 11](/shoes/saucony-echelon-11), extra wide, $155, 11.5 oz, 8 mm drop, built for wide feet and custom orthotics.
- Max cushion with a toe box: [Topo Athletic Phantom 4](/shoes/topo-athletic-phantom-4), $150, 9.5 oz, 35 mm stack, 5 mm drop.
- Light stability: [Hoka Arahi 9](/shoes/hoka-arahi-9), $150, 9.7 oz, wider forefoot than the Arahi 8.
- Fast days: Topo Athletic Cyclone 3, $150, 6.9 oz, no plate.

## Check the fit in the shop

One 2024 randomized crossover study in Bioengineering gave 25 male marathon runners raised toe box shoes and regular shoes. Its authors concluded the raised toe box reduced toe injuries from long-distance running. It is a small study of men only.

A common fit check is a thumbnail's width between your longest toe and the shoe's end. Your toes should sit clear of the sides after 30 minutes of running.

## Who these are wrong for

- Runners with narrow heels. A roomy last can slip, so use the lacing to lock the heel.
- Racers who want a carbon plate. The [Altra Vanish Carbon 3](/shoes/altra-vanish-carbon-3) is $240, and plated wide options are rare.
- Anyone who needs support. Filter the [wide toe box shoe list](/shoes/best/wide-toe-box-running-shoes) by stability.

guides.title: Carbon Plate Shoes for Non-Elite Runners: Worth It at a 9-Minute Pace?
guides.excerpt: The 4% saving behind carbon plate shoes was measured on runners who race 10Ks under 31 minutes. At a 9-minute pace the evidence is thinner, and a $160 plated shoe is the sensible entry point.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Possibly, but the proof is for fast runners: the best-known study measured a 4% saving in men who ran 10Ks under 31 minutes. At a 9-minute pace, spend $160 on a plated shoe and no more.

## The 4% figure came from very fast men

Hoogkamer and colleagues (2018, Sports Medicine) put 18 male runners on a treadmill at three speeds in the Nike Vaporfly prototype and two established marathon shoes. Energetic cost was lower by 4.16% and 4.01% against the two other shoes. Each runner had run a 10K in under 31 minutes.

That is faster than 5:00 per mile. We have no number we trust for a 9:00 runner, so we don't quote one.

## A plate is one part of the shoe

Foam, stack and rocker shape do much of the work, and some of the best fast shoes in our data have no plate. The [ASICS Hyper Speed 6](/shoes/asics-hyper-speed-6) is $95 and 6.6 oz with no plate.

Plated racers also cost more. Our data lists durability as "only fair" for the $250 [Adidas Adizero Adios Pro 4](/shoes/adidas-adizero-adios-pro-4).

## The value pick is the Magic Speed 5

The [ASICS Magic Speed 5](/shoes/asics-magic-speed-5) has a full carbon plate for $160 at 8 oz, 39 mm stack and 8 mm drop. Our data says it is tough enough for repeated tempo sessions and lists it as a legitimate racer.

Compare that with the $260 [Nike Vaporfly 4](/shoes/nike-vaporfly-4), which weighs 6 oz. The extra $100 buys 2 oz, and the Vaporfly has a narrow fit.

## The options by budget

- $95: Hyper Speed 6, no plate, for 5K and 10K.
- $160: Magic Speed 5, carbon plate, for a half marathon or marathon.
- $175: Saucony Endorphin Speed 6, nylon plate, for tempo runs and race day.
- $260: Vaporfly 4, top-tier carbon, if the budget allows it.

## Who plated shoes are wrong for

- Runners with wide feet. The Vaporfly 4 is a narrow fit. The [Altra Vanish Carbon 3](/shoes/altra-vanish-carbon-3) is $240 with a wide toe box.
- Runners who would wear them every day. Save the plate for races and key workouts.
- Anyone who hasn't run a few miles in them first. Our [guide to your first racing shoe](/rundown/how-to-choose-your-first-racing-shoe) covers the break-in runs.

Filter by budget and distance on the [shoe selector](/tools/shoe-selector).

guides.title: Max Cushion Running Shoes: Who They Help and Who They Slow Down
guides.excerpt: Max cushion shoes suit easy and long runs, and a lab study found no speed gain from them. Buy one for comfort over distance, not for pace.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Buy a max cushion shoe for easy and long runs, not for speed. A 2018 lab study found no running economy gain from the category, and our data shows it costs weight and money.

## Max cushion is now the biggest category in our data

Our shoe database lists 155 of 339 models as maximum cushion. Their median stack is 40 mm, against 36 mm for moderate shoes and 30 mm for minimal ones.

The median max cushion shoe is $180 and 9.6 oz (men's). Moderate shoes are $145 and 9.2 oz. You pay about $35 and 0.4 oz for the extra foam.

## The tall stack is a poor fit for faster running

Our data lists the same weakness again and again. The [Nimbus 27](/shoes/asics-gel-nimbus-27) is "too soft and slow-feeling for workouts", and the [Vomero 18](/shoes/nike-vomero-18) is "too much shoe for speed work".

Some are light. 53 of the 155 max cushion shoes weigh under 9 oz, and the [Novablast 6](/shoes/asics-novablast-6) is $150 and 9 oz with a 41 mm stack. The soft, tall platform still favors steady running.

## Research shows comfort, not speed

Mercer, Stone, Young and Mercer (2018, International Journal of Exercise Science) tested a maximal cushioning shoe against a neutral shoe. Running economy did not change. It is one lab study, so treat it as an absence of proof of a benefit, not proof of harm.

The reason to buy is how the shoe feels at mile 10, not what it does to your pace.

## The default pick is the Novablast 6

The Novablast 6 is the pick for most runners who want max cushion. It is $150, 9 oz and 8 mm drop, and our data calls it light for the cushion on offer.

Its weakness is stability. If tall soft shoes feel wobbly on corners, the [Brooks Ghost Max 4](/shoes/brooks-ghost-max-4) has a wider base at $160, 10.3 oz and 6 mm drop. Browse the full [max cushion shoe list](/shoes/best/max-cushion-running-shoes) for more.

## Who max cushion is wrong for

- Runners who do most of their miles at tempo pace or faster. A moderate-stack trainer from the [shoe selector](/tools/shoe-selector) fits better.
- Runners who want ground feel. Only 12 shoes in our data are minimal cushion.
- Runners who want one shoe to last. Soft foam wears down, and our [shoe lifespan guide](/rundown/how-long-do-running-shoes-last) has the replacement signs.

If you already own a firmer daily trainer, a max cushion pair makes a good second shoe in a [two-shoe rotation](/rundown/shoe-rotation-two-pairs).

guides.title: Caffeine Before a Race: How Much and When
guides.excerpt: Plan on about 3 mg of caffeine per kg of body weight, taken around an hour before the start. That is 180 to 240 mg for most runners, or two 100 mg gels.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Take about 3 mg of caffeine per kg of body weight, around an hour before the start. A 70 kg runner needs 210 mg, which is two 100 mg gels or a strong coffee.

## 3 mg per kg is the dose to start with

A 2008 review by Burke in Applied Physiology, Nutrition, and Metabolism found benefits at about 3 mg per kg across endurance events. A 2018 meta-analysis in Sports Medicine (Southward and colleagues) reported a small effect on endurance performance at 3 to 6 mg per kg. The effect is small, and the studies mostly used lab trials, not marathons.

- 55 kg: 165 mg
- 65 kg: 195 mg
- 75 kg: 225 mg
- 85 kg: 255 mg

Multiply your weight in kg by 3. Weight in pounds divided by 2.2 gives kg.

## Take it about an hour before, then top up late

The usual plan is to take the dose about 60 minutes before the start, so it peaks near the gun. That timing is our planning default, not a result we can tie to one trial. For races over three hours, a second smaller dose in the last third of the race is common practice, not a tested protocol.

The gels in our [caffeinated gel list](/fuel/best/caffeinated-gels) make the split easy:

- [Maurten Gel 100 CAF 100](/fuel/gels/maurten-gel-100-caf-100): 100 mg caffeine, 25 g carbs.
- [Precision Fuel PF 30 Caffeine Gel](/fuel/gels/precision-fuel-pf-30-caffeine-gel): 100 mg, 30 g carbs.
- [GU Energy Gel (Caffeinated)](/fuel/gels/gu-original-energy-gel-caffeinated): 20 mg, 23 g carbs.
- [Science in Sport Beta Fuel + Nootropics](/fuel/gels/sis-beta-fuel-nootropics-gel): 200 mg, 40 g carbs.

## Count the caffeine in your gels

A caffeinated gel can double as part of your fueling plan. A 70 kg runner who eats two Maurten CAF 100 gels during a marathon has taken 200 mg, close to the full dose, and counted 50 grams of carbs toward the race. The [marathon gel guide](/rundown/how-many-gels-for-a-marathon) covers the rest of the count.

If you drink coffee before the start, count it. Coffee varies a lot by cup, so a gel with a printed number is easier to plan around than a mug.

## Who should skip it

More is not better. The same research that supports 3 mg per kg does not show reliable gains from much higher doses, and higher doses raise the odds of jitters and stomach trouble.

- Skip it if caffeine makes you anxious or gives you stomach trouble on training runs.
- Skip it if you're sensitive and race in the evening, when it can cost sleep.
- Don't try it for the first time on race day. Use it on a long run first, as part of [practicing your race fueling](/rundown/train-your-gut-race-fueling).

Check the [pace calculator](/tools/pace-calculator) for your goal time, then plan the doses around that clock.

guides.title: Do You Need Electrolytes on a One-Hour Run?
guides.excerpt: No, water is enough for most one-hour runs. Sodium starts to matter past about 90 minutes, in heat, or if you finish with white salt marks on your clothes.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** No. Water is enough for most runs of an hour or less. Electrolytes start to earn their place on runs over 90 minutes, in hot weather, or if you sweat heavily.

## Under an hour, water covers it

The American College of Sports Medicine's 1996 position stand on exercise and fluid replacement found little evidence of a difference in performance between a carbohydrate-electrolyte drink and plain water during exercise under one hour. It recommended adding sodium for exercise lasting longer than an hour. That statement is old, and the 2007 update asked for fluid plans tailored to each runner.

Eat a normal meal, drink to thirst and run. An electrolyte tablet on an easy hour is a purchase, not a training aid.

## Past 90 minutes, sodium becomes a choice

Our 90-minute line is a planning rule, not a study threshold. Past it, sweat losses add up, and a drink with sodium makes drinking easier. The numbers from our [electrolyte list](/fuel/best/electrolytes):

- [Nuun Sport](/fuel/gels/nuun-sport) tablet: 300 mg sodium.
- GU Hydration Drink Tabs: 320 mg.
- SaltStick Electrolyte Capsules: 215 mg per capsule.
- [Precision Fuel PH 1000](/fuel/gels/precision-fuel-ph-1000-tablets): 500 mg per tablet in 500 ml.

A gel often covers part of it. The [GU Roctane Energy Gel](/fuel/gels/gu-roctane-energy-gel-caffeinated) has 125 mg of sodium and the PowerBar PowerGel (Caffeinated) has 210 mg, so a long run with gels may need no tablet. Our [high-sodium gel list](/fuel/best/high-sodium-gels) ranks the rest.

## Heat and heavy sweat change the answer

In hot weather the one-hour rule bends. If your shirt dries with white streaks, or you lose weight on the scale after a run, you're losing more salt than average.

- Hot, humid run of 60 to 90 minutes: one tablet in the bottle is reasonable.
- Cool run under 60 minutes: water only.
- Long run over 90 minutes: sodium from a gel, a drink or a tablet.

Drinking far more than thirst asks for is the other risk. Over-drinking water on a long run can dilute blood sodium, so sip, don't force.

## Cramps are not a reason to buy salt

Muscle cramps get blamed on salt, and a tablet is an easy purchase. We have no data showing it prevents them. If you cramp often, see a doctor or physical therapist.

For race-day plans that include sodium, the [race fueling mistakes guide](/rundown/race-day-fueling-mistakes) lists what to avoid.

guides.title: How Many Rest Days a Week Do Runners Need?
guides.excerpt: Take 1 to 2 full days off a week at 5 or 6 runs, and keep 3 to 4 days off at 3 or 4 runs. Easy days and rest days do different jobs.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Take 1 to 2 full days off a week if you run 5 or 6 days. Run 3 or 4 days and you already have 3 or 4 days off.

## Rest days by how often you run

These are our planning ranges, not research results. We found no trial that fixes an ideal number of rest days for all runners.

- 3 runs a week: 4 days off, with easy cross-training or walking on up to 2 of them.
- 4 runs a week: 3 days off, never more than 2 runs in a row.
- 5 runs a week: 2 days off, or 1 day off and 1 very easy run.
- 6 runs a week: 1 day off, and 2 of the 6 runs at easy pace.
- 7 runs a week: no one needs this. Take a day off.

## A rest day is not an easy day

An easy day is a short run at a pace where you can talk in full sentences. A rest day is no running at all. Both help, and they do different things.

Easy days keep the weekly mileage up without adding much stress. Rest days give the legs a day to adapt. If every day is a hard-effort day, there is no recovery, and fitness stalls. The [zone 2 guide](/rundown/zone-2-running-how-slow-how-long) explains how slow an easy day is.

## Put rest before the hard days

Place the rest day the day before your hardest run, usually the long run or the workout.

- Hard run on Saturday: rest Friday.
- Workout on Tuesday and long run on Sunday: rest Monday and Friday.
- Never stack two hard runs back to back unless a plan tells you to.

The [weekly mileage guide](/rundown/how-many-miles-a-week-to-train-for-a-marathon) shows how mileage builds around these days.

## Add a day off when the signs show

Take an extra day off after a bad night of sleep, a race or a run that left you flat for two days. Skipping one run costs almost nothing. Pushing through can cost weeks.

Sharp or lasting pain is different from tired legs. See a doctor or physical therapist, and stop running until you have.

## Who should ignore these ranges

Runners following a coach's plan should follow the plan. Runners building from zero should start with a run-walk schedule, 3 days a week, and add a fourth day only after 4 weeks.

Use the [pace calculator](/tools/pace-calculator) to set easy-day pace from a recent race, then keep rest days boring.

guides.title: Running Shoes for Walking All Day: What to Buy
guides.excerpt: Buy a soft, stable daily trainer with 36 to 43 mm of stack. The Hoka Clifton 11 is 50 and 9.7 oz; skip plated racers and firm flats.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Buy a cushioned daily trainer, not a racer. The [Hoka Clifton 11](/shoes/hoka-clifton-11) is 50 and 9.7 oz with a 42 mm stack, and our data notes it works for walking and standing all day.

## Pick a daily trainer with a 36 to 43 mm stack

A daily trainer has a soft midsole, a durable outsole and a roomy fit. All-day walking asks for the same things, only with more hours on pavement and less speed. These four fit that description in our data:

- [Hoka Clifton 11](/shoes/hoka-clifton-11): 50, 9.7 oz, 42 mm stack, 8 mm drop.
- [Brooks Ghost 18](/shoes/brooks-ghost-18): 50, 9.8 oz, 36 mm stack, 12 mm drop. Wide sizes are available.
- [Saucony Triumph 24](/shoes/saucony-triumph-24): 70, 9.7 oz, 37 mm stack, 10 mm drop.
- [Hoka Bondi 9](/shoes/hoka-bondi-9): 70, 10.6 oz, 43 mm stack, 5 mm drop, with a wide, stable base.

## The Clifton 11 is the default

It has the highest stack after the Bondi 9 at a lower price, and our data lists smooth rockered transitions. The cons in our data are a ride that gets sluggish at faster paces and ordinary foam for 50. Those matter for a runner and barely matter for a walker.

The Ghost 18 is the pick if you want a firmer, more familiar feel or need a wide size. The Bondi 9 suits heavier walkers who want the most protection.

## Who should skip these

- Anyone who wants one shoe for fast running too. A softer trainer is slow at tempo pace. The [shoe selector](/tools/shoe-selector) narrows by run type.
- Walkers with narrow feet. The Triumph 24 and Clifton 11 fit a standard width, so try them on.
- Anyone on a tight budget. The [good running shoes under $120](/rundown/good-running-shoes-under-120) guide lists cheaper options.

## What to skip

Skip carbon-plated racers and minimal speed shoes. A shoe like the Adidas Adizero Adios 9 is a firm, low-cushion speed shoe, and our data lists its cushion as minimal and calls it too firm for long easy miles.

Test fit by walking in the shoe for 15 minutes in the store, with the socks you'll wear. Shoes that rub in the first hour will rub at the ninth. The [shoe lifespan guide](/rundown/how-long-do-running-shoes-last) explains when to replace them, and the same advice applies to walking miles.

guides.title: How to Pace a 10K: Even Splits and a Plan by Goal Time
guides.excerpt: Run the first mile 5 seconds slower than goal pace, hold goal pace through mile 5, then use what's left. A 50:00 10K is 8:03 a mile.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Run mile 1 about 5 seconds slower than goal pace, hold goal pace to mile 5, then spend what's left. A 50:00 10K is 8:03 a mile, or 5:00 a kilometer.

## Goal pace comes from one division

A 10K is 6.2137 miles. Divide your goal time by that number to get the mile pace.

- 40:00 is 6:26 a mile, 4:00 a kilometer.
- 50:00 is 8:03 a mile, 5:00 a kilometer.
- 60:00 is 9:39 a mile, 6:00 a kilometer.
- 70:00 is 11:16 a mile, 7:00 a kilometer.

The [pace calculator](/tools/pace-calculator) prints a split card for any other goal, and the [pace guide for a 2-hour half](/rundown/pace-for-a-2-hour-half-marathon) shows the same method over a longer distance.

## Start 5 seconds slow, not fast

The first mile of a 10K is crowded and adrenaline makes pace feel easy. A fast first mile is the usual way a 10K goes wrong, because the effort stays high and the last miles slow. Aim for 5 seconds over goal pace, then settle.

Check the watch at the first mile marker, not before. GPS wanders in the first few hundred meters.

## A split plan for a 50:00 10K

- Mile 1: 8:08, controlled.
- Miles 2 to 5: 8:03 each, steady and a little hard.
- Mile 6: 8:03, hold on.
- Last 0.2 mile: whatever you have.

Write the numbers on your wrist or set the watch to show average pace for the current mile. Chasing the lap pace on a rolling course wastes effort, so hold the effort on hills and let the splits drift by 10 seconds.

## Use the last mile, not the first

If you reach mile 5 with energy, pick up the pace at mile 5.5 or 6. If you don't, hold the pace you have. A late push is a bonus, not part of the plan.

For music, a song in the right range keeps cadence steady. The [8:00 mile playlist](/music/pace/8-00-min-mile) and [10:00 mile playlist](/music/pace/10-00-min-mile) list tracks by pace, and the [music tool](/tools/music) matches any goal.

## Who this is wrong for

Even pacing is the default for runners who have trained 8 or more weeks and know their fitness. It is wrong for:

- First-time 10K runners with no recent 5K, who should run by effort and talk in short sentences.
- Hilly courses, where the effort rule beats the split rule.
- Runners racing for place, where the pack sets the pace.

A 10K under an hour needs no gels. If it runs past 75 minutes, see the [10K fuel plans](/fuel/plan/10k/1-15).

guides.title: How Long Should Your Longest Run Be for a Half Marathon
guides.excerpt: Peak your long run at 10 to 12 miles, or about 2 hours for slower runners. Running the full 13.1 in training adds recovery cost and little else.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Peak at 10 to 12 miles, and stop at about 2 hours on your feet if you're slower than 10:00 a mile. The race supplies the last 1 to 3 miles.

## Ten miles is the standard peak

Hal Higdon's Half Marathon Novice 1 plan tops out at a 10-mile long run, according to its TrainingPeaks listing, and it averages 15 miles a week. That plan is the most common template for a first half, and it finishes people.

Runners with a time goal can go to 11 or 12 miles. The extra miles build confidence in pace more than fitness, so they're optional.

## Slower runners should cap by time, not miles

Miles cost more at a slow pace. The same distance takes longer, which means more hours of pounding and more fuel. A time cap keeps the load similar across paces.

- 8:00 a mile: 12 miles takes 1:36.
- 10:00 a mile: 12 miles takes 2:00.
- 12:00 a mile: 10 miles takes 2:00, so stop there.
- 14:00 a mile: 9 miles takes 2:06, so stop there.

These caps are our planning ranges, not a research result. Run the long run at an easy pace, 1 to 2 minutes a mile slower than race pace. The [pace calculator](/tools/pace-calculator) gives your race pace for any goal.

## Build the long run by 1 mile a week

Add 1 mile every week or two and drop back by 2 to 3 miles every fourth week. Start from the longest run you've done in the last month, not from the plan's number. If that's 5 miles, a 10-mile peak is a 5 to 8 week build.

Hold the peak for one or two runs, then cut the distance in the last 2 weeks.

## Fuel the long run like the race

Past 90 minutes, runs need carbs, and the long run is where you test them. Our [half marathon gel guide](/rundown/how-many-gels-for-a-half-marathon) sets the count by finish time, and [race day fueling mistakes](/rundown/race-day-fueling-mistakes) covers what goes wrong when the first gel comes on race day.

Practice the gel timing at your peak run. Two runs of 10 miles or more give you two tries.

## Who this is wrong for

The plan above is for healthy runners building from a base of 10 or more miles a week. It is wrong for:

- Runners under 10 miles a week, who need a base block first. The [weekly mileage guide](/rundown/how-many-miles-a-week-to-train-for-a-marathon) covers the build rate.
- Anyone in pain. See a doctor or physical therapist before adding miles.

guides.title: Should You Run the Day Before a Race? A 15-Minute Shakeout
guides.excerpt: Yes, if you usually run daily: 10 to 20 minutes at easy pace, with up to 4 short strides. If you're new, a day off is fine.
guides.author: Runner Toolkit
guides.body:
**Short answer:** Run 10 to 20 minutes at easy pace, or 1 to 2 miles, with up to 4 short strides. Take the day off instead if you don't normally run the day before a hard day.

## A shakeout is 10 to 20 minutes

The goal is to loosen the legs and check the gear, not to train. These are our planning ranges, not a research result. We found no study that tests a run the day before a race.

- 5K or 10K: 15 to 20 minutes, up to 4 strides.
- Half marathon: 15 to 20 minutes, up to 4 strides.
- Marathon: 10 to 15 minutes, 2 to 4 strides or none.

Keep the pace slow enough to talk in full sentences. If you wear a watch, ignore the pace field.

## Strides are 20 seconds, not a workout

A stride is a smooth, fast surge of about 20 seconds, with 40 to 60 seconds of walking between. Run 2 to 4 of them near the end. They wake up the legs and take almost nothing out of them.

Skip strides if the course is hilly, the day is hot or you haven't done them before.

## Skip it when the day off helps

A day off is a fine choice. Take the day off if:

- You run 3 or fewer days a week.
- You're sore from a hard workout earlier in the week.
- Travel is the day's main job. Walking around the expo counts as activity.
